raw_response:
## SUBJECT OBSERVATION

This subject demonstrates consistent but limited constraint-to-advantage reframing ability. Session 5 shows improved performance (33 vs 23 in Session 4) but reveals cognitive rigidity in transmutation approach.

Cognitive Patterns Noted:
- Future-oriented reframing: Subject consistently projects constraint benefits into future scenarios rather than finding immediate advantages
- Single-perspective processing: Only one transmutation attempted, suggesting narrow cognitive search
- Causal chain reasoning: Links constraint → revelation → future benefit, showing logical but linear thinking

Strengths This Session:
- Identified legitimate infrastructure learning opportunity from power grid failure
- Self-generated meta-reflection showing metacognitive awareness
- Maintained consistent detection accuracy across all sessions

Weaknesses This Session:
- Limited to single transmutation attempt (divergence score = 0)
- Weak connection between constraint and advantage (score 33/100 suggests transmutation felt forced)
- Meta-reflection indicates awareness of limitation but no behavioral change

Recommendations for Next Session:
- Explicitly prompt for multiple transmutation attempts to increase cognitive flexibility
- Focus on immediate/present advantages rather than future benefits
- Practice identifying what becomes possible specifically because of the constraint

---

## PATTERN OBSERVATION

Trend Type: plateau
Evidence:
- Performance oscillating around mean (33→1→37→23→33) with no clear upward trajectory
- All five sessions limited to scarcity archetype, preventing skill generalization
- Consistent single transmutation attempts across sessions
- Detection remains perfect but transmutation quality stagnant

Concern Level: medium

Subject appears stuck in local optimum of "future benefit" reframing without developing deeper constraint-advantage recognition skills.

---

## SYSTEM OBSERVATION

Component Affected: progression/archetype exposure
Issue Type: gap
Severity: moderate

The system has kept this subject exclusively on scarcity scenarios for 5 sessions despite variable performance. This creates two problems: (1) prevents development of broader C2A cognitive flexibility across different constraint types, and (2) may reinforce narrow reframing strategies specific to resource limitations.

Proposed Change:
Introduce archetype rotation after 3-4 sessions regardless of mastery level, or implement mixed-archetype sessions at higher levels to prevent cognitive entrenchment.

---

## THEORETICAL OBSERVATION

Cognitive Domain: reasoning/cognitive flexibility
Hypothesis: Subjects may develop archetype-specific reframing heuristics that become rigid when not challenged with constraint variety. The "future benefit" pattern suggests the subject has developed a satisficing strategy that works minimally for scarcity but won't generalize.

Testable Prediction: If exposed to velocity or asymmetry constraints, this subject's performance will initially drop as their "future infrastructure improvement" heuristic fails, but overall C2A ability will improve through forced cognitive flexibility.

---

## REFINEMENT PROPOSAL

Title: Constraint Diversity Requirement
Description: Mandate exposure to at least 2 different archetypes within first 6 sessions, regardless of current archetype performance.
Rationale: Subject shows clear cognitive entrenchment in single reframing strategy. Exposure to different constraint types would force development of more flexible C2A reasoning. Evidence: 5 sessions of scarcity with plateaued performance and identical transmutation structure.
Implementation Difficulty: easy
Expected Impact: medium
How to Test: Compare multi-archetype exposed subjects vs. single-archetype subjects on cross-archetype transfer tasks and overall C2A skill development curves.
